query: How does Werkzeug's test machinery execute a WSGI application and return its response: what happens when the application raises through start_response or uses the old write callable, how is the response iterator handled and closed, and what changes when the caller asks for the output to be buffered?

operations.name: The environment is copied so application mutations do not leak into later requests
An exc_info passed to start_response is re-raised with its traceback
The write callable returned by start_response appends to a buffer
Buffered mode turns the iterator into a list and closes the application early
Unbuffered mode iterates only until a response has started and chains what was already read

dependencies.name: The application's close callable is discovered up front
A close callable is restored on the chained iterator only when the iterator was replaced
